title: Strict coefficient tensor complexes descend through K-flat localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $(S_n,q_n)_{n\geq1}$ an inverse sequence of commutative $R$-algebra sheaves, with $q_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$ an $R$-algebra map. Let $\mathscr S(S)$ be the category of systems of $S_n$-module sheaves $L_n$ with $S_{n+1}$-linear maps $L_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{q_n}L_n$, and compatible componentwise morphisms; restriction of scalars is [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Its kernels and cokernels are componentwise. Use sheaves of modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and derived scalar extension computed by K-flat complexes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

For a cochain complex $P$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], define $F(P)^i_n=P^i\otimes_RS_n$, with differential $d_P\otimes1$ and transition $1\otimes q_n$. This is a complex of strict systems. The assignment on chain maps and chain homotopies is componentwise tensor with $1$. On the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ of K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $F$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms of strict-system complexes. There is an exact functor
$$\mathcal F:D(R)\longrightarrow D(\mathscr S(S))$$
with a natural comparison $\mathcal F(Q_RP)\simeq Q_{\mathscr S}F(P)$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_R$, unique up to the unique comparison compatible with this normalization. These comparisons are independent of the K-flat representative and natural for derived morphisms represented by roofs in $\mathcal P_R$.

For every $n$, exact evaluation identifies $e_n\mathcal F(M)$ naturally with $M\otimes_R^LS_n$. Under this identification, the underlying transition is the quotient/coefficient-induced map: on $P$ it is $x\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes q_n(c)$. The maps for composite indices are the actual composites of these strict transitions. This asserts existence and descent of a functor into the ordinary derived category of strict systems, not merely a system of objects in the separate derived categories. No coefficient map is required to be flat or surjective, and no boundedness or geometric hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the natural algebra sequence from the adjacent compatibility ha by NatTrans.ofOpSequence. Use the concrete additive extension functor of [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction], followed by the ringed sequence equivalence of [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Its level comparison is the identity on sections after restriction along the identity coefficient identification. For a vertical arrow its naturality is exactly the identity-transition law of the strict system.

The section formula characterizing transition in [def-coef-semilinear-system-models] identifies it with horizontal restriction. Apply the existing extension transition_tmul formula: horizontal restriction followed by the identity vertical restriction sends s tensor x to q(s) tensor x, for every composite index, including the identity index. Additivity and functoriality hold before passing to complexes.

The existing extension_preserves proof of [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction] gives quasi-isomorphism invariance on K-flat complexes. The exact ringed sequence equivalence preserves homology, so the ordinary functor into sequence-site module sheaves also preserves these quasi-isomorphisms. In particular it preserves them on the resolving class with flat terms.

Use [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to resolve every complex. Transfer termwise tensor exactness to IsFlatOnSite by the existing siteSheafTensorRightIso. On the homotopy category, lift quasi-isomorphisms and use the invariance just proved; apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to obtain the pointwise universal derived pair, triangulated and computing on resolving complexes. Transfer its pointwise right Kan extension along the full essentially surjective homotopy quotient and the quotientCompQhIso to obtain precisely the cochain counit.

For each exact evaluation compose the cochain counit with its canonical exact-derived comparison and the termwise ordinary level isomorphism. This natural transformation is invertible on every resolving complex. Compare it with the scalar model counit from [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], also invertible there. The generic comparison_from_resolutions proof of [lem-cbc-derived-constant-tower-normalization] extends their quotient uniquely to a natural isomorphism. Its normalization is exactly the displayed evaluation_normalized equation.

Apply the same generic comparison_from_resolutions lemma to the actual counit and any competing counit invertible on the resolving class. It gives the unique normalized natural isomorphism required by Descent.unique, without assuming the competing pair universal. The lemma uses the right calculus on the homotopy category and [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class]; cancellation on a resolution proves uniqueness on all derived objects. Assemble all fields of Descent.
